exposure: Clinical practices leading to liability risk
Attending a vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC)
outcome: Amounts incurred in court decisions or pretrial settlements
cohort: The study analyzed 162 closed medical malpractice litigation cases that involved midwives insured by AIG between 2002 and 2011.
finding: The study identified 7 major categories of liability risk for midwives, with fetal/newborn complications or death being the most prevalent and attending a vaginal birth after cesarean being the least prevalent, and also examined the highest amounts incurred in court decisions or pretrial settlements related to adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: One of the 7 major categories of liability risk identified was attending a vaginal birth after cesarean.
